title: Ravina bar Shila
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned only in halakhah, and Rav Chisda received from him, as we find Rav Chisda citing Ravina bar Shila twice in [Sukkah 13a:4-6](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.13a.4-6), and also in [Moed Katan 17b:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.17b.7) and [Yevamot 68b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.68b.3). At Zevachim 36a in Hyman’s citation (compare [Zevachim 36b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.36b.8)) it reads bar Sila, and Hyman proposes bar Shila, as the statement is cited in the Kesef Mishneh, Hilkhot Pesulei HaMukdashin 14:9.[^3]

In [Pesachim 59a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.59a.13), Ravina speaks in the name of Rav Chisda. Hyman proposes that Rav Chisda is speaking in the name of Ravina bar Shila and cites Dikdukei Soferim for that reading.
In [Zevachim 89b:25](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.89b.25): “Ravina bar Shila said: The sacrificial portions of holy offerings,” etc.
In Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 2:3: “Rabbi Zeira said: Binah bar Shila recited [a baraita].”

notes.text: ב״פ is read as twice and כ״מ as Kesef Mishneh. Hyman’s only-in-halakhah assertion and proposed Shila/Sila and transmission reversals remain attributed. תני in the Jerusalem Talmud notice is the baraita-reciter role.

Two separate consulted Sukkah 13a passages have Rav Chisda reporting Ravina bar Shila. This does not by itself establish the universal “only in halakhah” assertion, or verify the Kesef Mishneh and Dikdukei Soferim readings reported by Hyman.

Rav Chisda cites Ravina bar Shila twice in Sukkah, on reeds for roofing and on bitter herbs. Yevamot gives “Ravina son of Rav Shila.” In the consulted Zevachim passage, on the next folio from the one Hyman gives, Rav Chisda cites Ravina bar Sila. Hyman proposes Shila on the basis of the Kesef Mishneh.
